answer_text:
# 🥛 Calcium-Containing Foods

Calcium is the most abundant mineral in your body and a major component of your bones and teeth. Since your body can't make calcium on its own, it's essential to consume calcium-rich foods to meet your daily needs.

Calcium is used for numerous functions, including building bones and teeth, muscle contraction, blood clotting, maintenance of cell membranes, and nerve transmission.

---

## 🧀 1. Dairy Products
When you think of high-calcium foods, dairy products like **milk, yogurt, and cheese** probably come to mind first. Dairy foods are some of nature's most concentrated sources of calcium, and many come packaged with other bone-building nutrients like protein, phosphorus, and (when fortified) vitamin D.

- **Swiss Cheese** – ~1,175 mg per cup (diced)
- **Yogurt (low-fat, fruit)** – ~235 mg per 6 oz container
- **Yogurt (plain, whole milk)** – ~206 mg per 6 oz container
- A **3 cm cube of hard cheese** has as much calcium as a cup of milk.
- **Skim milk** products provide as much calcium as whole milk with the added advantage of less fat and cholesterol.

---

## 🐟 2. Fish & Seafood
**Canned salmon or canned sardines** are excellent non-dairy sources of calcium.

- **Canned pink salmon** – ~241 mg per 3 oz
- **Sardines** – rich in calcium (especially when bones are consumed)

---

## 🥦 3. Vegetables & Greens
Many plant foods are also calcium-rich, including **greens, beans, tofu, nuts, and seeds**.

- **Turnip greens** – ~209 mg per cup (cooked)
- **Kale, collard greens, bok choy** – good sources
- Some greens like **spinach and chard** are higher in oxalic acid, but **kale, collard greens, and bok choy** contain lower amounts, so the calcium they contain is likely better absorbed.
- **Broccoli** – a good calcium source

---

## 🫘 4. Legumes & Beans
- **Black beans** – ~239 mg per cup (raw)
- **Cowpeas (black-eyed peas)** – ~211 mg per cup (cooked)
- **Beans and tofu** (if processed with calcium sulfate) are excellent non-dairy calcium options.

---

## 🥜 5. Nuts & Seeds
Most vegetables, legumes, nuts, seeds, and dried fruit contain some calcium.

- **Almonds** – one of the best nut sources of calcium
- **Sesame seeds** – very high in calcium
- **Chia seeds** – a good plant-based source

---

## 🍊 6. Fortified Foods & Beverages
**Calcium-fortified soy, almond, and rice beverages**, as well as **calcium-fortified orange juice**, are great non-dairy options (check the nutrition labels).

- Fortified cereals
- Fortified breads

---

## 🌾 7. Grains & Other Foods
- **Enriched bagels** – ~217 mg per bagel
- **Tofu (made with calcium sulfate)** – a significant plant-based source

---

## ⚠️ Tips for Better Calcium Absorption
- Calcium-rich foods and calcium-fortified foods are the preferred choices for obtaining calcium because additional nutrients like **vitamin D** in milk can contribute to bone development and the prevention of osteoporosis.
- Check food labels to find out the percentage of calcium in processed foods. Every **10% of calcium listed on the label** is equivalent to approximately **100 mg of calcium**.
- The calcium content listed for most foods is estimated and can vary due to multiple factors, so check the food label to determine how much calcium is in a particular product.
